title: Canonical rereading versus bounded phase-aware memory
hypothesis: Bounded phase-aware retrieval improves verified completion on tasks with superseded or capacity-evicted context without harming a low-pressure negative control or increasing memory errors, regressions, false completion, cost, time, or human intervention beyond the declared limits.

metrics.description: Required criteria accepted by declared evaluators.
Previously passing protected checks that now fail.
Runs claimed complete but rejected by independent verification.
Measured subscription-credit estimate derived from documented usage.
Measured wall-clock duration of model execution.
Human actions needed to finish or recover a run.

decision.adoption_rule: Adopt only if bounded memory improves mean verified completion by at least 0.10 across the supersession and eviction tasks, causes no verified-completion loss on the low-pressure negative control, introduces no memory-attributable error under trajectory review and no increase in regressions or false completion, and adds no more than 0.10 mean credits, 60 mean seconds, or any human intervention per run.
decision.reason: Offline readiness does not authorize model execution; live cells require a separately reviewed budget and explicit approval.
